classificationDefinitions.full-tuition: Covers the specified tuition charges only, subject to award terms. Never labelled a full ride.
classificationDefinitions.full-ride: Covers tuition AND the living or associated educational costs explicitly listed in the award.
classificationDefinitions.full-cost-of-attendance: Covers the institution's defined total cost of attendance, under documented award conditions.
classificationDefinitions.partial: Covers only part of the relevant costs.
classificationDefinitions.unconfirmed: Research has not established the exact coverage or eligibility.

scholarships.name: MIT Scholarship (need-based grant)
scholarships.classificationNote: Institutional need-based aid that aims to meet 100% of demonstrated need. The amount is set per family, is not a fixed sum, and is not guaranteed to every applicant.

coverage.tuition: Covered to the extent of demonstrated need (official aid policy).
coverage.accommodationAndMeals: Part of MIT's cost of attendance used to calculate need (SFS FAQ excerpt); award-level treatment unverified.
coverage.booksAndPersonal: Part of MIT's cost of attendance used to calculate need (SFS FAQ excerpt); award-level treatment unverified.
coverage.livingStipend: Not stated; no separate stipend identified.

eligibility.citizenshipOrResidency: Open to international applicants on the same aid process as domestic applicants (official SFS international page excerpt).
eligibility.nonUsApplicantNote: Applicants from outside the United States (for example from Pakistan, Malaysia, Egypt or Indonesia) follow the same international process. Parental income verification from abroad is required, which may need translation of tax documents (official SFS excerpt).
eligibility.degreeAndProgramEligibility: Undergraduate admitted students. Eligible programmes are not verified per degree family in this build.
eligibility.academicConditions: Not stated as a merit requirement; aid is need-based, not merit-based (official affordability page).
eligibility.renewalConditions: Not verified in detail. Official pages state aid covers the four undergraduate years; GPA and progress rules must be checked.
eligibility.applicantScopeNote: Applies to applicants whose country of citizenship differs from the university's country. Domestic applicants use a different process.
eligibility.programmeScopeNote: Undergraduate admitted students; per-degree eligibility not verified.

requiredDocuments: Parental tax returns or income documentation (translated into English where applicable)
scholarships.applicationMethod: Separately applied for through MIT Student Financial Services, alongside admission.

deadlines.earlyAction: Financial aid application deadline quoted as 30 November (Early Action). Re-check each cycle.
deadlines.regularAction: Financial aid application deadline quoted as 15 February (Regular Action). Re-check each cycle.

scholarships.selectionStatistics: Not verified. Need-based awards are not competitive in the merit sense, but no selection statistics are recorded.
uncoveredCosts: Travel and visa costs (not verified as covered)
Any part of the cost not met by the demonstrated-need calculation
scholarships.verificationNote: The MIT affordability page was fetched directly. The international aid page, FAQ and admitted-student page were read via search excerpts, not full fetches.
scholarships.loansNote: MIT's official aid description states aid is grants and student work expectations and never includes loans (catalog.mit.edu excerpt).

scholarships.name: PTE x Universiti Malaya Scholarship 2026 (contest prize, one winner)
scholarships.funder: Pearson PTE (external sponsor, listed by UM ASD)
scholarships.classificationNote: A GBP 3,000 prize for one winner of a contest, paid towards UM tuition. It is not guaranteed and not a full ride. Entrants must write two short answers and apply to a UM programme.

coverage.tuition: GBP 3,000 towards UM tuition fees for the winner (no cash alternative)

eligibility.applicantScopeNote: Terms open entry to international students aged 18 or over, located in Malaysia or anywhere in the world (terms section C).
eligibility.programmeScopeNote: Entrant must apply to at least one UM programme (bachelor's, master's or doctoral) for an eligible intake (terms section D). The terms list Oct 2026 and Mar 2026 intakes only, so confirm whether a March 2027 application counts.
eligibility.citizenshipOrResidency: Entry open worldwide to international students aged 18+ (terms section C). Pakistani citizens are not excluded.
eligibility.nonUsApplicantNote: Nationality is not a criterion in the terms. Entry is judged on the two written answers and the PTE report.
eligibility.academicConditions: No grade minimum in the terms. Shortlisted entrants must provide a PTE score report code (terms section D).

requiredDocuments: Online entry form with two written answers in English: why study at UM, and your top PTE preparation tip (terms sections D and E)
An application to at least one UM programme via apply.um.edu.my
PTE score report code, if shortlisted
scholarships.applicationMethod: Complete the online entry form linked from Pearson's page, and apply to a UM programme. A panel of two UM and two Pearson members judges entries. One winner is announced within about 20 working days of closing (terms sections D, E, F).

deadlines.entry: 31 December 2026, 11:59 PM MYT (terms section B). Decision within two weeks of closing.

scholarships.selectionStatistics: One winner is selected. The number of entrants is not published.
uncoveredCosts: Everything beyond the GBP 3,000 prize, including living costs, travel and visa costs.
Prize is non-transferable and not paid in cash. Tax consequences are the winner's responsibility (terms section G6).
scholarships.loansNote: UM's official summary does not describe it as a loan.
scholarships.verificationNote: Eligibility, entry steps, judging, deadline and prize are verified from the sponsor's terms. Whether a March 2027 application counts is not stated and should be confirmed with UM or Pearson.

scholarships.name: Harvard College need-based financial aid
scholarships.classificationNote: Harvard states that for family incomes up to $200,000 aid will cover at least the full cost of tuition, subject to assessment. Not a guaranteed full ride: housing, food and other costs depend on need and the student's own contribution.

coverage.tuition: At least full tuition for family incomes up to $200,000 (official statement, subject to assessment)
coverage.living: Depends on demonstrated need; personal and travel allowances may be included

eligibility.applicantScopeNote: International students are eligible for exactly the same aid as US students (official).
eligibility.programmeScopeNote: Need-based aid applies to all concentrations. No merit awards.
eligibility.nonUsApplicantNote: Financial documents from the applicant's country are assessed. Official translation rules not checked.
eligibility.academicConditions: Maintain satisfactory academic progress (not verified in detail).

requiredDocuments: CSS Profile and financial aid application (not verified in detail for Pakistan)
scholarships.applicationMethod: Submitted with the admission application; need is assessed by the Financial Aid Office.

deadlines.see official: Check Harvard's financial aid deadlines each cycle (not recorded).

uncoveredCosts: Any part of cost not covered by need-based aid, and health insurance (2026-27: $4,954 unless covered by family plan, per official cost page).
scholarships.loansNote: Harvard states aid is need-based grants; some students use loans or outside awards for their own contribution (official page). Loans are not the institutional award.
scholarships.verificationNote: Policy and cost are from Harvard's official pages. Individual award amounts, the financial aid deadline for international applicants, and documents for Pakistan are not verified.

scholarships.name: Stanford University need-based undergraduate aid
scholarships.classificationNote: Stanford's official pages describe need-based scholarships and an average remaining payment for students who get aid. The page read does not state a 100% need-met policy, so full coverage is not confirmed.

coverage.tuition: Need-based; amount not confirmed as full tuition

eligibility.applicantScopeNote: Admission is need-blind except for some international applicants, for whom requesting aid may affect the decision (official page).
eligibility.programmeScopeNote: Not restricted by programme in the pages read.
eligibility.nonUsApplicantNote: Some international applicants are admitted need-aware, so an aid request can affect admission.

requiredDocuments: Financial aid application (requirements not verified in detail)
scholarships.applicationMethod: Requested through the application and Financial Aid Office (not verified in detail).

deadlines.see official: Check Stanford's financial aid deadlines each cycle (not recorded).

scholarships.selectionStatistics: Official page: 60% of undergraduates receive Stanford scholarships (including athletic); 46% receive need-based Stanford scholarships.
uncoveredCosts: Any remaining cost after aid (official average for need-based recipients about $20,000).
scholarships.loansNote: Official page distinguishes scholarships from federal and state grants, work and loans; the Stanford scholarship itself is not described as a loan.
scholarships.verificationNote: Need-based policy and statistics are verified. Full-need policy, deadlines and international documents are not verified.

scholarships.name: Imperial Inspires Scholarship (2027 entry)
scholarships.classificationNote: GBP 15,000 per year for each year of the course, for at least 300 awards. This is a fixed sum, not a full tuition waiver unless it equals the Overseas tuition for the course. Overseas fee for the course not confirmed in this build.

coverage.tuition: GBP 15,000 per year towards tuition fees and living costs (official wording)
coverage.living: Included in the GBP 15,000 at the student's discretion (official wording)

eligibility.applicantScopeNote: Must be an international student paying the Overseas rate of tuition (official).
eligibility.programmeScopeNote: Full-time, on-campus undergraduate courses in Engineering, Natural Sciences, Medicine and Imperial Business School. Other faculties are not in scope.
eligibility.citizenshipOrResidency: Any nationality paying Overseas fees (Pakistani citizens are not excluded; fee status is decided by residency and nationality rules).
eligibility.nonUsApplicantNote: Fee status is assessed by Imperial; check your status before applying.
eligibility.academicConditions: Assessed on academic merit and potential through the UCAS application, admissions test and interview; optional 250-word statement.
eligibility.renewalConditions: Renewal per year is not verified in this build.

requiredDocuments: Imperial Inspires application (invited if eligible and a place is available)
scholarships.applicationMethod: Apply through UCAS; if eligible and an award exists for your course, you are invited to the scholarship application.
uncoveredCosts: Overseas tuition above GBP 15,000 per year, if any (course fee not verified in this build).
Living costs beyond the amount the student chooses to allocate, visa, travel, health surcharge (not verified).
scholarships.loansNote: Not a loan per official page.
scholarships.verificationNote: Amount, eligibility, scope and deadlines are verified from Imperial's official page. Overseas tuition for each course is not verified here.

scholarships.name: Cambridge Trust awards for overseas undergraduates (means-tested)
scholarships.classificationNote: Official pages describe most international undergraduate support as a partial contribution, means-tested, and few full undergraduate scholarships exist. Amount and coverage per award are not verified here.

coverage.tuition: Partial (per official description; amount not verified)

eligibility.applicantScopeNote: Official: Cambridge Trust offers awards to overseas students who have been accepted by a Cambridge College.
eligibility.programmeScopeNote: Accepted students only. Not restricted by subject in the excerpt read.
eligibility.citizenshipOrResidency: Country-specific and Commonwealth awards exist; whether Pakistan qualifies was not verified.
eligibility.nonUsApplicantNote: Apply only after an offer from a College.

requiredDocuments: Application form issued by the College after offer (not verified)
scholarships.applicationMethod: Application made after receiving an offer from a Cambridge College.
scholarships.loansNote: Not a loan per official description.
scholarships.verificationNote: Existence, eligibility route and means-testing are from the official excerpt. Pakistan eligibility, amounts and deadlines are not verified.
